# Set F — operational definitions of redundant / replaced / single contamination

**Workstream:** WS2 (protocol items 2.1–2.5) · **Reviewer comments:** R2-M6, R1-M3, R1-m4
**Generated by:** `scripts/144_contamination_type_module.py`, `scripts/145_generate_set_F.py`
**Data:** `data/benchmarks/set_F/` · **Results:** `results/revision/set_F/`

> **Prior work first (protocol §8 rule 5).** Non-redundant contamination being
> under-estimated by marker-gene methods was reported by **Cornet & Baurain
> (2022)** and quantified across taxonomic ranks by **Cornet et al. (2024)**.
> This work does not discover that phenomenon. Its contribution is (i) measuring
> it for a k-mer/deep-learning estimator alongside three modern tools on a
> leakage-free, fully-crossed benchmark with bp-level ground truth, and (ii)
> resolving the taxonomic-distance axis at six ranks in the practically relevant
> 0–20 % contamination band.

---

## 1. What the source papers actually define

### Cornet & Baurain 2022, *Genome Biology* 23:60 — Supplementary Note 1
Two genomes, a **master** (acceptor) and a **sub-genome** (donor), are annotated
with Prodigal; OrthoFinder infers orthologous groups; groups containing exactly
one sequence from each genome (single-copy orthologues) are randomly sampled.
Two flavours are built, each at 5 % of total proteins:

* **non-redundant** — genes of the master genome are **replaced** by the
  corresponding sequences of the second genome;
* **redundant** — genes of the master genome are **duplicated** by genes from
  the sub-genome (the master keeps its own copy).

Their result: CheckM "overestimated redundant contamination levels but does not
detect replaced or single contamination".

### Cornet et al. 2024, *Applied Microbiology* 4(1):9 — the CRACOT framework
(preprint bioRxiv 2022.11.14.516442). Generalises to **three** event types and
**six taxonomic ranks (phylum → species)**. All quotations below are **verbatim
from the CRACOT preprint** (re-verified against the primary text on 2026-07-27):

* Definitions — "The first type is **redundant** contamination that occurs when
  the contaminant sequence is redundant with an homologous genomic sequence of
  the expected organism. The second type is **replaced** contamination that is
  similar to the first one, but with the genuine sequence of the expected
  organism **lacking from its genome**. The third type is **single**
  contamination that occurs when the contaminant sequence has **naturally no
  homologous sequence** within the genome of the expected organism."
* Orthology — Prodigal V2.6.3 then **OrthoFinder V2.5.4**. "Common proteins were
  defined as proteins present in only one copy for both the main and slave
  genome in the OG while single proteins were **singletons of the slave genome**."
* Event construction — "**Duplicated** contamination events were fished from the
  pool of common OGs, and the corresponding gene sequences of the slave genome
  were **added to the end of the last contig** of the master genome (with a serie
  of five 'N' added to either side of the gene). **Replaced** contamination events
  were also fished from the pool of common OGs but **slave genes replaced the
  genuine genes within the main genome**. **Single** contamination events were
  fished from the pool of **singletons** of the slave organism, and the
  corresponding gene sequences were added to the end of the last contig of the
  master genome, as above."
* Pairing — "for one specific taxonomic rank, ranging from phylum to species.
  When a rank is selected, the two genomes should belong to the same taxon at
  this rank, but have a **different taxonomy starting with the next rank**."
  (NCBI Taxonomy; 705 references from class Clostridia and genus *Lactobacillus*.)

Their result: "only **redundant** contamination is accurately estimated". CheckM
"overestimated the redundant CL … but quite logically, **does not detect replaced
or single** contamination"; CheckM2 "largely **overestimated** the redundant CL at
all ranks and, as for CheckM, **underdetected replaced and single** contamination
events".

### GUNC — Orakov et al. 2021, *Genome Biology* 22:178 (third prior-work anchor)
**Citation correction (2026-07-27).** An earlier draft of this document attributed
the sentence below to Cornet et al. 2024. It is **GUNC's**, not Cornet's. It is
retained here because GUNC's simulation is *bp-level* and therefore the closest
published analogue to ours, and because it independently establishes the same
phenomenon that R2-M6 raises:

> "Non-redundant contamination was simulated by **replacing part of an acceptor
> genome by a size-matched contaminant fraction of a donor genome**; to simulate
> redundant contamination, **surplus donor fragments were added to complete
> acceptor genomes**. We observed that CheckM systematically **overestimated
> completeness and underestimated contamination** for genomes with simulated
> non-redundant contamination, largely **independent of the taxonomic level** of
> source genome divergence."

So the phenomenon has been reported **three** times before this work (Cornet &
Baurain 2022; Orakov et al. 2021; Cornet et al. 2024). Our contribution is
quantification and speed, not discovery (protocol §8 rule 5, item 9.11).

---

## 2. Our operational definitions (exactly what is implemented)

MAGICC's ground truth is expressed in **base pairs against the dominant genome's
full reference length**; Cornet's framework is expressed in **genes**. We
therefore implement bp-level analogues that preserve the *mechanism*
distinguishing the three types, and state the adaptation rather than hiding it.

Let **A** = acceptor (dominant) reference, **D** = donor (contaminant) reference.

| Step | Implementation |
|---|---|
| Gene calls | Prodigal 2.6.3, `-p single`, on the unmodified reference FASTA |
| Orthology | **Reciprocal best DIAMOND blastp hits** (DIAMOND 2.1.24, default sensitivity), e-value ≤ 1e-5, ≥ 30 % identity, ≥ 50 % query coverage |
| `common` genes | donor genes **with** an RBH partner in the acceptor |
| `singleton` genes | donor genes **without** an RBH partner in the acceptor |
| Donor *block* | a maximal run of consecutive same-class donor genes on one donor contig, plus the intergenic DNA between them; blocks break at the first gene of the other class and at contig ends |

| Type | Donor material added | Acceptor treatment | Mechanistic consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **REDUNDANT** | blocks of **common** genes | untouched | every transferred marker is now present **twice** (once from A, once from D) → the marker-duplication signal marker-based tools are built on |
| **REPLACED** | blocks of **common** genes | a **size-matched** amount of acceptor sequence is deleted, anchored on the acceptor's own RBH partners of exactly those transferred genes and grown around them until deleted bp == added bp | every transferred marker is present **exactly once**, but from the wrong organism; total assembly size unchanged; true completeness falls by the replaced fraction |
| **SINGLE** | blocks of **singleton** genes | untouched | **no** marker duplicated and **none** replaced — the assembly simply gains foreign accessory DNA |

**Invariant enforced in code and verified per sample:** for REPLACED, *every*
acceptor copy of a replaced marker is deleted in full (`acceptor_mandatory`
intervals are never truncated by the size-matching step). Validation check
`replaced_deletes_every_acceptor_marker_copy` fails the build otherwise.

### Ground truth (MAGICC's production convention, unchanged)
```
completeness  (%) = retained dominant bp  / dominant FULL reference bp x 100
contamination (%) = total contaminant bp  / dominant FULL reference bp x 100
```
Both are **measured** from the emitted contigs, never assumed.

---

## 3. Deliberate deviations from the source papers, and their direction of bias

1. **RBH instead of OrthoFinder orthogroups.** OrthoFinder over ~1,300 genomes ×
   1,624 pairings is not affordable inside this revision; RBH is the standard
   surrogate for one-to-one orthology between two genomes. RBH is *conservative*
   (it misses some divergent orthologues), so the singleton pool is slightly
   inflated. That makes the **SINGLE** class marginally *easier* for marker-based
   tools than a true singleton set would be — so any under-estimation measured for
   SINGLE is a **lower bound**.
2. **Blocks (multi-gene segments + intergenic DNA), not bare CDSs.** Contaminating
   DNA arrives in a real MAG as contigs, and all four tools consume nucleotide
   FASTA. Transferring bare CDSs would produce an assembly no assembler could
   emit and would be unfair to every tool.
2b. **Donor material is emitted as its own contigs and shuffled into the assembly**,
   fragmented on the same empirical contig-length model as the dominant — *not*
   appended to the end of the acceptor's last contig with `N` padding, as CRACOT
   does. Appending places foreign and native genes on one physical contig, which
   no assembler produces and which would systematically penalise contig-aware
   detectors (GUNC) while flattering contig-agnostic ones. This choice follows
   GUNC's fragment-level simulation and is the fairer test.
3. **Contamination expressed in bp, not % of proteins**, because that is the
   denominator the manuscript, its ground truth and all four tools use (R1-M4).
4. **The acceptor reference is treated as one concatenated sequence** (as
   `magicc.fragmentation.read_fasta` already does throughout this project), so the
   surviving pieces after a REPLACED excision are re-concatenated before
   fragmentation. This is the same class of artificial junction the production
   generator already creates between reference contigs; it is not new here.
5. **Acceptor genomes are complete but realistically fragmented** (target
   completeness 1.0, quality tier drawn per reference from
   {medium, low, highly_fragmented}), matching Cornet's use of complete acceptor
   genomes while keeping MAG-like contig structure. Realised completeness spans
   56–100 %.

---

## 4. Independent verification that the definitions do what they claim

The three types are verified by a scan that knows **nothing** about how each
sample was built: Prodigal + `hmmsearch --cut_tc` against this project's own
single-copy core-gene profiles (`85_bcg.hmm` / `uacg.hmm`) applied to the
finished Set F FASTA files, counting core-gene **families observed ≥ 2 times**.

| contamination type | mean duplicated SCG families | Δ vs uncontaminated control |
|---|---|---|
| none (control) | 0.00 | — |
| **redundant** | **11.53** | **+11.53** |
| replaced | 0.33 | +0.33 |
| single | 0.44 | +0.44 |

n = 126 assemblies (6 per type × distance cell, 18 controls).
`results/revision/set_F/set_F_marker_duplication_validation.tsv`.

Only REDUNDANT inflates marker duplication — exactly the Cornet semantics. An
earlier implementation of the REPLACED excision left acceptor copies behind and
this scan caught it (replaced showed +10.6 duplicated families); the bug was
fixed and the invariant is now asserted per sample.

## 5. Taxonomic distance is a measured gradient, not just a GTDB label

Percentage of donor genes with an RBH orthologue in the dominant
(`set_F_distance_summary.tsv`):

| distance | n pairs | mean % orthologous | median | p05 | p95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| species (different assembly, same species) | 129 | 87.96 | 88.81 | 68.50 | 99.07 |
| genus (different species) | 105 | 66.85 | 66.57 | 43.75 | 85.43 |
| family (different genus) | 100 | 45.04 | 48.87 | 23.10 | 60.69 |
| order (different family) | 100 | 30.14 | 29.34 | 16.02 | 46.70 |
| class (different order) | 101 | 21.36 | 21.51 | 5.49 | 35.93 |
| phylum (different class) | 107 | 15.67 | 15.42 | 5.36 | 24.62 |

## 6. Set F composition, seeds and provenance

* **1,900 samples** = 100 reference genomes × 6 taxonomic distances × 3
  contamination types (1,800) **+ 100 uncontaminated controls** (one per reference).
* Fully crossed: every reference appears once in every cell, with the **same**
  target contamination level and the **same** fragmentation tier, and (for
  REDUNDANT and SINGLE) a **byte-identical dominant assembly**. Type and distance
  contrasts are therefore paired within reference and within contamination level.
* Contamination ladder **1, 2, 3, 5, 7.5, 10, 12.5, 15, 17.5, 20 %** — ten
  references per level by seeded permutation, emphasising the practically relevant
  band (Reviewer 2). Mean realised contamination 9.25 % over the 1,800 contaminated
  samples (median 7.50 %, range 0.38–20.00 %).
* **Entirely inside the training domain** (contamination % ≤ completeness %,
  protocol §4.4a): 0/1,900 violations; completeness floor enforced at 55 %.
* **Seeds:** master `SET_BASE = 8_200_000`; per-sample `seed_dominant`,
  `seed_contaminant`, `seed_event` recorded in `generation_metadata.tsv`
  (48 columns, satisfies WS7.7 / R1-m15).
* **Leakage:** dominants **and** contaminants drawn exclusively from
  `data/splits/test_genomes.tsv`. Provenance audit with GCA↔GCF cross-mapping
  through `data/gtdb/filtered_genomes.tsv` (277,183 assemblies):
  **100/100 dominants and 519/519 contaminants in TEST, 0 in TRAIN, 0 in VAL**
  (519 = the donors whose sequence was actually transferred, drawn from a
  1,222-genome eligible test-split donor pool) —
  `results/revision/provenance/set_F_provenance_audit.json`,
  `set_F_overlap_summary.tsv`, `set_F_dominants.txt`, `set_F_contaminants.txt`,
  `set_F_sha256_manifest.txt` (1,907 files). **DISJOINTNESS VERDICT: PASS.**
* **Verification:** FASTA contig counts and bp match metadata exactly (0/1,900
  mismatches); 0 constraint violations; deleting samples and re-running
  regenerates them **byte-identically** with metadata unchanged
  (`scripts/145b_setF_determinism_check.sh`).

### Known limitations of the design, stated up front
1. **Restricted dominant pool.** A fully-crossed design requires each reference to
   have a test-split partner at all six ranks; 4,532/9,999 test genomes qualify and
   they are concentrated in well-sampled lineages. The 100 selected references
   (round-robin over families to maximise breadth) span 8 phyla / 13 classes /
   52 families / 63 genera, median genome size 3.20 Mbp (0.65–7.73). Set F does
   **not** cover CPR/DPANN or archaea; those are covered by Sets C_clean/D_clean.
   The alternative — different dominants per distance — would confound taxonomic
   distance with genome composition, the exact error the WS1 decision rule was
   corrected for.
2. **Shortfall.** 109/1,800 samples could not reach their target contamination from
   the donor's eligible territory; 39 of those are SINGLE at species distance,
   where a conspecific donor has few singleton genes (median relative shortfall
   0.1 %, p90 50.4 %). Ground truth is the *observed* contamination, so these
   samples remain valid; `set_F_cells_sensitivity_no_shortfall.tsv` re-reports every
   cell with samples > 5 % relative shortfall removed and the conclusions are
   unchanged.
3. **Cross-phylum contamination is not a Set F cell** — Cornet's ranks stop at
   phylum. Cross-phylum contamination is covered by Sets B_v2 and E.
